Tim Johnson, Executive Director of the PFPF, presented the October 1, 2023 actuarial valuation report for the fund. He discussed the current funding policy for the pension and said the upcoming employer contribution for next fiscal year will be $178.1M. The net present value of the future sales tax funding stream is $1.37B. The pension funding plan assumes a 4.25% growth rate in sales surtax revenues while the actual rate for the year was 9.3%. The plan assumes a net return on assets of 6.5%; the actual rate for last year was 13.7%. The City experienced a savings of $97.5M on its annual contribution because of the new present value of the future sales tax collection. The plan’s overall funded percentage is 44.72%. He reported that beginning later this year the date of the City’s annual employer contribution payment will be moved up from December 1 to October 1 and the amount of the actuarial contribution will be netted against the funding the City provides from pooled cash to the PFPF to make the retiree pension payments during the year.

President Salem asked about the growth in the annual employer contribution amount and the estimated length of the sales surtax for the pension. Mr. Johnson said 2056 is the estimated date for full funding to be reached (earlier than the 2060 full term of the tax) and the sales tax would sunset when that is achieved. Mr. Salem said the City budget would be devastated if the sales tax had not been adopted to pay the unfunded pension liabilit
